clusters.name: Body Dysmorphic Disorder (BDD)
items: Preoccupation with perceived slight or unnoticeable physical defect (DSM p.271)
Repetitive behaviors or mental acts in response to appearance concerns (DSM p.271)
Clinically significant distress or impairment (DSM p.271)
Not better explained by eating disorder concerns (DSM p.272)

clusters.name: Hoarding Disorder
items: Persistent difficulty discarding or parting with possessions regardless of value (DSM p.277)
Perceived need to save items and distress associated with discarding (DSM p.277)
Accumulation cluttering active living areas (DSM p.277)
Significant distress or functional impairment / unsafe environment (DSM p.278)

criteria.thresholds: BDD: Preoccupation 3–8 hours/day (DSM p.272); Hoarding: persistent accumulation (DSM p.277)
subtypes: BDD insight specifiers: good/fair, poor, absent/delusional (DSM p.272)
Hoarding insight specifiers: good/fair, poor, absent/delusional (DSM p.278)

epidemiology.prevalence: BDD: 2.4% adults, 1.9-2.2% adolescents (DSM p.273-274); Hoarding: 1.5-6% (mean 2.5%) (DSM p.279)
epidemiology.sex_ratio: BDD: ~1:1 overall (2.5% F vs 2.2% M) (DSM p.274); Hoarding: ~1:1 community (DSM p.279)
epidemiology.onset_age_typical: BDD: peak 12-13 years, mean 16-17 (DSM p.274); Hoarding: onset 15-19 years (DSM p.279)
comorbidities: BDD: MDD, SAD, SUD (DSM p.274, p.277)
Hoarding: MDD (30-50%), SAD, GAD, OCD (20%) (DSM p.281; Dulcan p.368)
epidemiology.prognosis: BDD: chronic without treatment (DSM p.274); Hoarding: chronic and progressive (DSM p.279)

etiology.genetic: BDD heritability 37-49% (DSM p.274); Hoarding family reports >50%, heritability ~50% (DSM p.279)
etiology.neurobiology: CSTC loops (StahlNeuro p.539-540); BDD: OFC dysfunction, detail-processing visual bias (DSM p.273); Hoarding: vmPFC and ACC dysfunction (DSM p.280)
etiology.environmental: BDD: child abuse/neglect, appearance teasing (DSM p.274); Hoarding: stressful/traumatic life events (DSM p.279)

first_line: High-dose SSRIs: Fluoxetine 20-80mg/d, Sertraline 50-200mg/d, Fluvoxamine 50-300mg/d (StahlKids p.202, 232, 446; Dulcan p.380)
key_side_effects: SSRIs: Gastrointestinal distress, activation, insomnia, sexual dysfunction (StahlKids p.202, 232, 446)
Clomipramine: Anticholinergic, sedation, weight gain, QTc prolongation (StahlKids p.132)
treatment.monitoring: Clomipramine: Baseline & dose-titration ECG (QTc monitoring), BP, pulse (StahlKids p.132; Dulcan p.380); SSRIs: Suicidality, behavioral activation (StahlKids p.202)

items: CY-BOCS / CY-BOCS II: Clinician-administered 5-domain severity rating scale (Dulcan p.374)
COIS: Child OCD Impact Scale for functional impairment (Dulcan p.375)
HRS and CIR: Hoarding Rating Scale & Clutter Image Rating for environment clutter (מקור: הקשר רחב)
key_numbers: CY-BOCS: 5 domains rated 0-4 (time, interference, distress, resistance, control) (Dulcan p.374)
CY-BOCS II: Adds explicit avoidance assessment (Dulcan p.374)

items: OCD: BDD focus limited to appearance; Hoarding in OCD driven by contamination/harm obsessions (DSM p.275, 280)
Eating Disorders: Concern limited to body fat/weight (DSM p.275)
Organic brain lesions: TBI, stroke, FTD, Prader-Willi causing hoarding (DSM p.280)
Shubo-kyofu & Koro & Olfactory Reference Disorder (DSM p.274, 276)
key_numbers: 26%: Rate of hoarding symptoms in pediatric OCD cases (Dulcan p.368)
33%: Proportion of BDD patients with delusional/absent insight (DSM p.272)

high_yield: Muscle dysmorphia occurs almost exclusively in males with steroid use risk (DSM p.271-272).
Delusional appearance beliefs are diagnosed as BDD with absent insight, not Delusional Disorder (DSM p.108, p.276).
BDD has 4x higher suicidal ideation and 2.6x higher suicide attempts vs controls (DSM p.274-275).
BDD involves OFC dysfunction and detail-processing bias; Hoarding involves vmPFC and ACC dysfunction (StahlNeuro p.539-540; DSM p.273, p.280).
Clomipramine requires mandatory ECG monitoring for QTc prolongation at baseline and titration (StahlKids p.132; Dulcan p.380).
